chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

The Ihram (entering the state of ritual consecration for Hajj) is not valid except after a prescribed (fard) prayer. If you enter Ihram after it, following the Taslim (conclusion), then the meaning in this narration is excellence and recommendation, because it is most excellent for a person to enter Ihram immediately after a obligatory prayer, as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did. And the most excellent of the obligatory prayers is that it be after the Dhuhr prayer. And that which indicates this is that Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, the narrator of this hadith, narrated after quoting this report what the Imam (peace be upon him) said: 'And if it is a voluntary prayer, you pray two rak'ahs and enter Ihram after them.' So we know that he meant by the first (narration) what we mentioned of excellence, otherwise it would be contradictory. And that which indicates this also...
ai.seo_question: When is the best time to enter Ihram for Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi highlights the juristic preference (*istihbab*) for entering Ihram immediately after an obligatory prayer, particularly Dhuhr, aligning with the Prophetic tradition of combining ritual purity with pilgrimage intent. The commentary clarifies that this timing maximizes spiritual reward rather than serving as a strict condition for validity, as evidenced by the permissibility of entering Ihram after voluntary prayers without contradiction. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on optimizing acts of worship through their connection to established ritual frameworks.
